sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains why the lulav is not taken on Shabbat during Sukkot when the first day falls on Shabbat, contrasting the revelation of the encompassing light on Shabbat with the need for the lulav during the Temple era versus the exile.

translations.translation: A)
And this is [the reason] why the first festival day of Sukkot that falls on Shabbat, the lulav does not override Shabbat,
for taking the lulav is in order to draw down the aspect of the encompassing light
(of the sukkah)
into inwardness; therefore on Shabbat, when the encompassing light shines in the aspect of inwardness
(due to the nature of Shabbat),
there is no need
(so much)
for taking the lulav,
and therefore Rabbah's decree suffices to set aside the taking of the lulav.
And that in the time of the Holy Temple they would take it even on Shabbat,
is because there are several levels in encompassing lights,
and through taking the lulav in the time of the Temple they drew down a higher encompassing light than the encompassing light drawn on Shabbat by itself
(that Shabbat is sanctified and stands [by itself]68)
and also outside the Land
(in the time of the Temple).
But in the time of the exile,
even through taking the lulav it is impossible to draw down the higher encompassing light,
and what they draw down now is only the aspect of the encompassing light that is drawn through Shabbat.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the drawing down of the encompassing light of the sukkah is a close preparation for the future revelation of the inner aspect of Atik, which will be revealed in the future redemption through Moshiach.

translations.translation: And behold, as stated above,
"In sukkot you shall dwell,"
the drawing down of the encompassing light of the sukkah,
is a close preparation for "every native in Israel" to shine in the future,
the revelation of the aspect of the true encompassing light,
the aspect of the inner aspect of Atik.
For this is the innovation in the revelation of the future,
that now all revelations are only from the aspect of the external aspect of Atik, but in the future there will be a revelation of the aspect of the inner aspect of Atik69.
And this is what is said70
"Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" — that they will learn the Torah of Moshiach from the mouth of Moshiach,
whose concept is the aspect of the inner aspect of Atik
[for this is that Moshiach is above even Adam HaRishon,
and as it is written71
"He shall be high and exalted and lofty exceedingly,"
"exceedingly" (me'od) are the letters of Adam (Adam), but in a permutation that indicates [being] without [the letter] lamed-gimmel,
meaning above even Adam HaRishon72].
And this is "In sukkot you shall dwell... every native...,"

that the drawing down of the encompassing light of the sukkah is a close preparation for the revelations of the future redemption through our righteous Moshiach, may he come and redeem us and lead us upright to our land,
and there we will perform before You our obligatory sacrifices according to the commandment of Your will,
speedily, truly.
